method_card.title: Past Holidays and Experiences
method_card.content:
This lesson focuses on describing past holidays using the perfect tense. The highest-yield grammar point in this theme: whether to use haben or sein as auxiliary.

GermanEnglish
ich bin gefahrenI went / travelled (fahren — movement)
ich bin geflogenI flew (fliegen — movement)
ich bin gegangenI went / walked (gehen — movement)
ich bin geschwommenI swam (schwimmen — movement)
ich bin gebliebenI stayed (bleiben — state-change)
ich habe besuchtI visited (besuchen — transitive)
ich habe gegessenI ate (essen — transitive)
ich habe getrunkenI drank (trinken — transitive)
ich habe gemachtI did / made (machen — transitive)
ich habe gesehenI saw (sehen — transitive)
am Strand liegen / gelegento lie on the beach / lay
Sehenswürdigkeiten besichtigento visit sights
Fotos machen / gemachtto take photos / took

Grammar focus — haben vs sein: Most verbs use haben. Use sein for: (1) movement verbs — fahren, fliegen, gehen, laufen, schwimmen, kommen, reisen; (2) state-change verbs — bleiben, werden, einschlafen, aufwachen. Examples: Ich bin nach Spanien gefahren (sein — movement) vs Ich habe ein Museum besucht (haben — transitive, no movement). The past participle always goes to the end of the clause.

Grammar focus — past participle position: The past participle sits at the very end: Ich bin mit dem Flugzeug nach Rom geflogen. NEVER split the participle from the end: Ich bin nach Rom geflogen mit dem Flugzeug ✓ is slightly odd but acceptable; Ich bin nach Rom mit dem Flugzeug geflogen ✓ is standard — participle at end always.

Model paragraph: Letzten Sommer bin ich mit meiner Familie nach Italien geflogen. Wir haben ein altes Schloss besucht und viele Fotos gemacht. Ich bin jeden Tag im Meer geschwommen und habe leckeres Eis gegessen. (Last summer I flew to Italy with my family. We visited an old castle and took lots of photos. I swam in the sea every day and ate delicious ice cream.)
steps: Learn the key holiday activity verbs — classify each as haben or sein in the perfect tense
Master past participles: weak (ge-…-t: gemacht, besucht) and strong (ge-…-en: geflogen, gegessen, geschwommen)
Always place the past participle at the end of the clause
Build full sentences combining sein/haben + country prepositions + past participles

exam_context.frequency: Highest-yield perfect-tense topic — past holidays appear in writing tasks, picture cards and speaking prompts

worked_examples.question: Why does 'Ich bin nach Spanien gefahren' use bin, not habe?

steps.label: Identify the verb
steps.content: fahren = to travel/go. Ask: is this a movement verb?

steps.label: Apply the rule
steps.content: fahren is a movement verb (it describes travel from one place to another). Movement verbs take sein as auxiliary in the perfect tense.

steps.label: Check the participle position
steps.content: The past participle gefahren goes to the end of the clause. Auxiliary (bin) stays at position 2.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich bin nach Spanien gefahren. — sein because fahren is a movement verb; gefahren at the end.

worked_examples.question: Translate: 'We visited a museum and ate pizza.' (Decide haben or sein for each verb.)

steps.label: First verb: besuchen (to visit)
steps.content: besuchen is transitive (takes a direct object — the museum). It is not a movement verb. Use haben: wir haben … besucht. Past participle: inseparable prefix be- → no ge- → besucht.

steps.label: Second verb: essen (to eat)
steps.content: essen is transitive. Use haben: wir haben … gegessen. Past participle: strong verb → gegessen.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Wir haben ein Museum besucht und Pizza gegessen.

worked_examples.question: Spot the error: 'Ich habe nach Spanien gefahren.' What is wrong and why?

steps.label: Identify the verb
steps.content: fahren = to travel. It is a movement verb.

steps.label: Apply the rule
steps.content: Movement verbs take sein, not haben. The auxiliary habe is wrong here.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Correct sentence: Ich bin nach Spanien gefahren. — Replace habe with bin.

bronze.question: Match the German past-tense forms to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct auxiliary
sentence_parts: ich mit meiner Familie nach Spanien

gaps.rule: Perfect tense auxiliary — sein for movement verbs
gaps.correct_explain: bin is correct. Fliegen is a movement verb, so the perfect tense uses sein.

wrong.habe: habe is wrong — fliegen is a movement verb and takes sein, not haben.

gaps.correct_explain: geflogen is the irregular past participle of fliegen (to fly). It goes at the end of the clause.

wrong.fliegen: fliegen is the infinitive. You need the past participle: geflogen.
wrong.gefahren: gefahren is the participle of fahren (to drive/travel), not fliegen.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct auxiliary and past participle

gaps.rule: Perfect tense auxiliary — sein for bleiben (state-change)
gaps.correct_explain: sind is correct. Bleiben (to stay/remain) is a state-change verb and takes sein.

wrong.haben: haben is wrong — bleiben is a state-change verb and takes sein, not haben.

gaps.correct_explain: geblieben is the irregular past participle of bleiben (to stay).

wrong.gebleibt: There is no form gebleibt. Bleiben is irregular: geblieben.

bronze.question: Which sentence is correct? (haben vs sein)
What does 'Als wir in Spanien waren, haben wir jeden Tag am Strand gelegen' mean?
options: When we were in Spain, we lay on the beach every day
When we were in Spain, we swam in the sea every day
Although we were in Spain, we stayed in the hotel
When we go to Spain, we will lie on the beach

bronze.source_text: Letzten Sommer war das Wetter fantastisch. Wir haben am Strand gelegen und Fotos gemacht.
model_answers: Last summer the weather was fantastic. We lay on the beach and took photos.

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: Last summer I **flew** to Greece and **swam** in the sea every day.
sentence_parts: Letzten Sommer bin ich nach Griechenland

gaps.correct_explain: geflogen is the irregular past participle of fliegen. It takes sein as auxiliary.

wrong.gefahren: gefahren means 'travelled/drove' — it is the participle of fahren, not fliegen.

gaps.rule: Past participle of schwimmen — takes sein
gaps.correct_explain: geschwommen is the irregular past participle of schwimmen (to swim). Note: schwimmen takes sein.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Weil es sonnig war, haben wir am Strand geschwommen.
silver.error_type: Perfect tense auxiliary — sein vs haben
silver.explanation: Schwimmen is a movement verb. Movement verbs take sein in the perfect tense, not haben. Correct: sind wir geschwommen.
silver.translation: Because it was sunny, we swam on the beach.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: It rained, so we went to the museum.

distractor_labels.haben: wrong auxiliary — gehen is a movement verb and takes sein, not haben.

silver.source_text: The weather was bad. We visited a castle and bought souvenirs.
model_answers: Das Wetter war schlecht. Wir haben ein Schloss besucht und Souvenirs gekauft.

gold.source_text: When we were in Spain, the weather was fantastic. We swam in the sea every day and visited many places of interest.
model_answers: Als wir in Spanien waren, war das Wetter fantastisch. Wir sind jeden Tag im Meer geschwommen und haben viele Sehenswürdigkeiten besucht.

Check: als + verb-final (waren), preterite war, sein for schwimmen (movement), haben for besuchen (transitive), past participles at clause end, no ge- on besucht (inseparable be-). Accept valid alternatives. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: Because the weather was bad, we stayed in the hotel.

distractor_labels.ist,: wrong tense — this describes the past. Use war (preterite), not ist (present).
distractor_labels.haben: wrong auxiliary — bleiben takes sein, not haben.
distractor_labels.bleiben: wrong form — you need the past participle geblieben, not the infinitive.

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are staying at a campsite in Germany. The site manager asks how your holiday has been so far.

bullets.prompt: Say where you travelled from and how you got here.
bullets.model_answer: Ich bin aus England gekommen. Wir sind mit dem Auto gefahren.
bullets.note: sein + kommen (movement); sein + fahren (movement); mit dem Auto (dative after mit)

bullets.prompt: Describe what you did yesterday — visit a town and eat in a restaurant.
bullets.model_answer: Gestern sind wir in die Stadt gegangen und haben in einem Restaurant gegessen.
bullets.note: sein + gehen (movement); haben + essen (transitive); in einem Restaurant (dative after in for location)

bullets.prompt: Say the weather was great and you swam in the lake.
bullets.model_answer: Das Wetter war super und ich bin im See geschwommen.
bullets.note: war (preterite of sein); sein + schwimmen (movement verb); im See (dative)

bullets.prompt: Ask whether there is a shop on the campsite and what time it opens.
bullets.model_answer: Gibt es einen Laden auf dem Campingplatz? Um wie viel Uhr öffnet er?
bullets.note: es gibt + accusative (einen Laden — masculine); öffnet er (question with inversion)

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German describing a recent holiday. Include: where you went and how you travelled, what you did (at least two activities using the perfect tense), your opinion, and what you would do next time.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about a past holiday. Mark on: Communication (all bullet points addressed?), Range of language (perfect tense with both haben and sein — has the student demonstrated knowledge of the auxiliary split?, preterite war/hatte, opinion with weil/obwohl, connectives), Accuracy (sein for movement verbs, haben for transitive verbs, past participles at clause end, noun capitalisation, case). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

gold.source_text: If I could choose, I would go on holiday somewhere where the sun always shines, because I hate cold weather.
